summary: Implement Issue #1 kernel lifecycle: every protocol/startup/dispose terminal transition kills and evicts the owning process tree, waitReady is bounded by the eval deadline and caller AbortSignal, Runtime.dispose() is idempotent-terminal so post-dispose eval rejects without spawning.

pointers: M2: a corrupt JSON frame from the kernel kills and evicts the process tree
M2: a non-object frame from the kernel kills and evicts the process tree
M2: an unknown frame type from the kernel kills and evicts the process tree
M2: a frame with a wrong request id from the kernel kills and evicts the process tree
M2: a wrong ready version terminates the startup path once, kills, and evicts
M2: a silent kernel that never sends ready is killed by the startup deadline
M2: aborting during the ready handshake kills the kernel and rejects with cancel
M2: disposing during the ready handshake settles the waiter and kills the kernel
M2: dispose is terminal and a later eval is rejected without spawning

steps: Read AGENTS.md, issue-repair-playbook.md, architecture.md, milestones.md, project-status.md, review-findings.md, development-memory README and the existing runtime/tests/kernel before mutating; reference decision for host-side lifecycle is mechanism-absent (no local ref/rlm or ref/prime-agent source checkout exists).

Reproduced all three defects on the frozen base with a temp script: protocol fault left the kernel PID alive (orphan kept the Node event loop open), a 400ms timeout did not bound a silent ready wait, and eval after dispose still attempted a spawn (kind=spawn).

Implemented unified terminal transitions: Kernel.handleExit now always kills the process tree before onExit eviction; Kernel.waitReady races the ready promise against the effective cell timeout and the caller AbortSignal through handleExit; Kernel.dispose rejects a pending ready and marks exited; RlmRuntimeImpl is terminal after dispose so eval rejects closed without spawning; ready version mismatch was rerouted through handleExit.

Added deterministic regression tests: raw-frame injection through sys.__stdout__ for corrupt JSON/non-object/unknown frame/wrong request id, sitecustomize-shadowed silent startup for ready deadline/abort/dispose plus bad ready version, and a terminal-dispose test with a missing interpreter; every lifecycle test asserts the real OS PID is gone via tasklist.
Ran pnpm typecheck, pnpm build, focused tests and the full offline suite before staging the candidate.

evidence.note: Protocol-fault PID stayed alive, ready wait did not settle within 1.5s under a 400ms timeout, and eval after dispose attempted spawn (kind=spawn) — all three defects reproduced on the frozen base.
tsc emit plus tsdown produced lib/index.mjs.

37/37 tests pass, including corrupt JSON, non-object, unknown frame, wrong request id, bad ready version, silent ready deadline, ready abort, ready dispose and terminal dispose; each lifecycle test asserts the real kernel PID disappeared.
45 tests: 43 pass, 2 skipped (RLM_LIVE_SMOKE-gated profile smoke), 0 fail.

limitations: The ready startup deadline reuses the effective cell timeout (input.timeout ?? config.timeout) as its own budget; startup and cell execution are not charged against one shared deadline and no separate startup-timeout option was added.

Protocol-fault coverage drives the host parser by having a cell write raw frames through sys.__stdout__; the unmodified production kernel never emits malformed frames, so these tests validate host defensive behavior only.

Silent-startup coverage shadows sitecustomize through PYTHONPATH with a PID marker; it depends on Python importing sitecustomize during interpreter startup and on the Windows-specific tasklist PID probes already used by the suite.

The synchronous-throw spawn() path (for example a non-executable interpreter command) still settles via rejectReady without the unified handleExit eviction; it predates this Issue and is out of scope.
No clean-Profile live smoke was run for this candidate (RLM_LIVE_SMOKE not set); lifecycle acceptance is proven by the deterministic offline suite only.

summary: Successor closure of Issue #1 kernel lifecycle on top of the first candidate: Windows tree-kill no longer relies on a bare PATH taskkill (absolute System32 path, async error and non-zero close listened, direct-child kill fallback, one kill attempt per kernel); one effective timeout is now the total deadline from Runtime.eval entry shared by waitReady and evalCell (no 2x worst case, no public startupTimeout); waitReady gained explicit settled/readyDone guards with synchronous timer/listener cleanup as low-cost defense for the resolveReady-to-finally window. Frozen acceptance (kill+evict on bad frames, ready deadline+abort, PID gone after terminal transitions, terminal dispose, PID-checking regressions) stays intact; daemon/public provider/snapshot/restore/storage remain rejected.

pointers: M2 Issue#1 successor: a taskkill startup failure falls back and never crashes the host
M2 Issue#1 successor: startup and cell share one total deadline
M2 Issue#1 successor: a late abort after a settled eval cannot evict the idle kernel

steps: Read AGENTS.md, the issue-repair playbook, the development-memory README, review-findings.md, the original implementer record and the frozen acceptance list; read the canonical refs rlm/source @ 854e688fbba9d8f8989e3da9989812e4b6dfe270 and prime-agent/source @ 6179a608f394d0858d463e40d648df0def6dbb7a (orphan-process-journal.ts killOrphanProcess) plus the rlm reference subprocess.py startup/stop pattern before mutating.

Reproduced the reviewer/coordinator finding on b1f13ae: on Windows child_process.spawn of a missing command returns first and then emits an unlistened async error; Kernel.kill spawned bare taskkill with no error listener. Verified with Node v24 on this host: unhandled error exits the process, a listened error surfaces ENOENT then close (-4058).

Wrote three red tests against b1f13ae before any implementation: (a) taskkill startup failure under bogus SystemRoot+PATH with guarded restore asserts no host crash and a fallback-settled kernel PID; (b) bounded startup (0.5s pressed ready) plus a slow cell under one 1200ms budget asserts total elapsed < 1600ms, PID gone and a fresh session works; (c) a late abort after a settled eval must not evict the idle kernel.

Implemented the fixes: resolveTaskkill() reads SystemRoot??C:\\Windows at kill time; killWin32() spawns the absolute path with NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1, listens error and non-zero close and falls back to child.kill() exactly once; kill() is idempotent via killStarted; RlmRuntimeImpl.eval computes one deadline and waitReady/evalCell consume the same budget; waitReady has settled/readyDone guards with synchronous cleanup in finish/finally.

Adaptation/rejection notes: adopted absolute-System32 taskkill + NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath + /T /F from the prime-agent orphan reaper but used async spawn with error/close listeners instead of its blocking spawnSync so terminal paths never block and never crash on a missing killer; kept /T /F tree semantics and pid targeting; rejected the rlm reference separate _startup_timeout (no public startupTimeout per frozen scope) and its graceful shutdown frame/daemon/sandbox cleanup (V1 keeps direct kill + fallback; no daemon, no journal, no public Kernel provider).

Ran gates before staging: red proofs on b1f13ae (taskkill run interrupted the test process; shared-deadline run measured 1881ms for a 1200ms budget), then pnpm typecheck, pnpm build, node --test tests/rlm-loop.test.ts, pnpm test and pnpm check:memory. The record is staged with the material change and the staged/range gates were validated at commit time without rewriting any existing record line.

evidence.note: The unlistened async spawn error interrupted the test process instead of completing, reproducing the coordinator Windows child_process.spawn finding; no fallback fired and the kernel PID was left alive.

evidence.note: 1881ms wall time for a 1200ms budget (0.5s bounded startup + full cell timeout), proving the ~2x worst case.

evidence.note: tsc emit plus tsdown produced lib/index.mjs; lib/ stays gitignored.
40/40 tests pass, including the three successor regressions; every lifecycle test still asserts the real kernel PID disappeared.
48 tests: 46 pass, 2 skipped (RLM_LIVE_SMOKE-gated profile smoke), 0 fail.

limitations: The taskkill-failure fallback kills only the direct kernel child; /T tree semantics hold when taskkill starts, but if it cannot start, kernel descendants are not tree-killed (the V1 kernel spawns no children today).

The shared-deadline regression uses bounded wall-clock timing (0.5s pressed startup + 1.2s budget, asserting < 1.6s); deterministic on this host but still timing-sensitive under extreme CI load; no fake timers were introduced.

The Windows taskkill test swaps process.env.PATH and SystemRoot inside a guarded try/finally and restores them; it does not leak state but relies on the suite existing Windows-only tasklist PID probes.

The resolveReady-to-finally window is provably unreachable for macrotask timer/abort events (microtasks finish before the next event); the added settled/readyDone guards are defense-in-depth and do not extend the state machine.
No clean-Profile live smoke was run (RLM_LIVE_SMOKE not set), same as the original candidate; no Job Object/daemon/journal/public Kernel provider was added (frozen non-goals).
The pre-existing synchronous-throw spawn settle path (rejectReady without unified handleExit eviction) is untouched and remains out of scope, as the original author recorded.
